page: Microsoft Azure D16ls_v7 is a low-memory general-purpose virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. Operating on the x86_64 architecture under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the system provides 16 dedicated vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. Memory capacity is configured at 32.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per virtual processor. The processor features 480 MB of L3 cache along with hardware acceleration instructions, including AVX-512, Intel AMX (tile and int8), and cryptographic primitives like AES and SHA-NI. The instance includes no discrete graphics processing units and features no onboard local storage, necessitating networked storage solutions for disk persistence.

Benchmark evaluations indicate consistent compute and compression throughput. The instance recorded a multi-core stress-ng metric of 18136.46 and a PassMark CPU score of 30370.06, placing it within median multi-threaded baseline tiers. Single-threaded throughput displays strong performance, achieving 35.31 GB/sec in gzip compression and 14.95 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression, both in the top 25 percent of tested systems. Memory bandwidth registers 134.42 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 55.39 GB/sec for writes. The integration of AMX enables 350.22 tokens per second during lightweight 135M parameter model text generation, though throughput moderates to 18.04 tokens per second on 7B models.

Hardware tradeoffs center on memory density and the omission of local ephemeral storage. By scaling memory to 2.0 GB per vCPU instead of traditional higher-memory configurations, the instance maximizes CPU resource density for processing-heavy workloads that do not demand large RAM pools. Cost efficiency is optimized for environments where paying for excess unutilized memory would be wasteful. Because zero local scratch storage is bundled, workloads rely on networked disk I/O, which must be factored into deployment architecture. The server is well fitted for compression pipelines, stateless containerized microservices, CPU-bound batch processing, and web serving tiers.
description: Microsoft Azure D16ls_v7 is a compute-focused general-purpose virtual machine equipped with an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Managed via Microsoft Hyper-V, the system provides 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores and 32.0 GB of memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The platform incorporates AVX-512 and Intel AMX matrix extensions alongside 480 MB of L3 cache, omitting local disk storage and discrete GPUs. In benchmarking, the instance demonstrates mid-tier multi-core compute throughput and memory bandwidth, alongside strong single-threaded gzip compression at 35.31 GB/sec and fast lightweight LLM generation reaching 350.22 tokens per second. The constrained memory density reduces memory overhead for tasks that do not demand extensive RAM capacity, making the server suitable for compute-heavy stateless microservices, compression routines, CI/CD processing, and web applications utilizing networked storage.
